1.gloss: homeostasis — override frequency measured in hours to weeks

needs.title: Food / caloric intake
needs.definition: Adequate calories and nutrients; failure kills in weeks or disables in months.
needs.description: Short-horizon bodily survival. Without adequate calories and nutrients, death follows within weeks (starvation) or is accelerated within months (deficiency disease).

needs.title: Water / fluid balance
needs.definition: Potable water in sufficient quantity, and the aquifers and systems that deliver it.
needs.description: Humans die of dehydration in 3-5 days without water. Unlike food, there is almost no storage buffer in the body. This makes water threats faster-acting and more politically volatile than food threats.

needs.title: Air / breathable environment
needs.definition: Air below the toxic threshold, ambient and occupational, indoor and outdoor.
needs.description:
- Failure runs on two clocks: acute events — gas releases, smog episodes, confined-space oxygen depletion — that injure or kill within minutes to days, and chronic exposure to particulates, combustion products and mineral fibres that shortens life over years to decades with no datable moment of harm. 

- The need spans two axes the regulatory system splits: ambient versus occupational (street air and workplace air sit with different authorities, and the dose is usually higher on the occupational side), and indoor versus outdoor (household cooking smoke is inside the need, not adjacent to it). Greenhouse gases are treated as a cross-cutting climate concern rather than a threat to this need directly.

needs.title: Shelter & thermoregulation
needs.definition: Enclosure that holds body temperature inside survivable bounds against heat and cold.
needs.description: Short-horizon survival need: a body loses to hypothermia in hours, to hyperthermia in hours-to-days, and to exposure-driven infection within days. Shelter is the buffer. History is a record of that buffer being destroyed faster than it can be rebuilt.

needs.title: Sanitation & disease
needs.definition: Separation of human waste from water, food and living space, and the disease load when it fails.
needs.description: Short-horizon survival threat: pathogens (bacterial, viral, parasitic) exploiting density, filth, war, and contact between previously isolated populations.

needs.title: Sleep / circadian regulation
needs.definition: Enough uninterrupted sleep, at the right point in the day-night cycle.
needs.description:
Thinner historical record than food or water. Sleep leaves no ruins, no
famine registers, no archaeological layer. Most of what follows is 20th
century onward — either because sleep loss was weaponized deliberately, or
because industrial and electric technology made circadian disruption a mass
condition for the first time. Pre-industrial sleep disruption (illness, cold,
predators, infant care, war) certainly existed but is not well documented as
a distinct threat category — folded into other tier-1 threats instead.

**The structural property that separates this need from the other five.**
Sleep requires nothing to be supplied. Food, water, air and shelter all fail
through **non-provision** — something must be produced, treated, delivered or
built, and the failure is that it wasn't. Sleep requires only that
interference be **removed**. That single asymmetry explains most of what
follows. It is why sleep has no ministry, no scheme, no budget line and no
procurement pipeline: there is nothing to buy. It is why every entry in the
India section below is *someone else's activity* — an employer's roster, a
discom's load schedule, a landlord's roof, a neighbour's generator, a
platform's dispatch algorithm — rather than an absent service. And it is why
the harm is systematically misfiled: a need that fails by imposition rather
than by scarcity has no natural claimant, so its damage is recorded under
whatever it later causes.

**A distinction this file must hold throughout: clinical vs imposed.** Total
or primary insomnia is a medical condition with a diagnostic pathway, however
poorly resourced (see the measurement note at the end of the India section).
Insufficient and poor-quality sleep in an otherwise healthy person is the far
larger band, and it is not a disease — it is an exposure. Collapsing the two
is what routes the entire problem to clinicians, where the environmental band
cannot be treated, instead of to the parties who impose it. Almost everything
below concerns the second category.

needs.title: Violence protection
needs.definition: Protection of the body from deliberate harm by others, private or state.
needs.description: A buffer against unpredictable future threats to body, claims, and resources — surviving today isn't enough if you can be destroyed tomorrow.

needs.title: Rule of law & property/contract rights
needs.definition: Claims and agreements that survive arbitrary power through a predictable, appealable process.
needs.description: A buffer against unpredictable future threats to claims and resources. Rule of law converts "what I hold, I might lose to arbitrary power" into a predictable, bounded, appealable process. When it fails, ownership and agreements become contingent on who holds power, not on codified right.

needs.title: Financial / economic continuity
needs.definition: The storage medium for the safety buffer — money, savings, banks — not failing under the buffer.
needs.description: A buffer against unpredictable future threats to resources. Money, savings, and banks are the storage medium for that buffer; this need is about the medium itself failing — through inflation, bank collapse, default, confiscation, or fraud — independent of any single threat to the resources it stores.

needs.title: Employment / livelihood security
needs.definition: The channel converting labour into resources staying open, suddenly or structurally.
needs.description: A buffer against unpredictable future threats to resources. Livelihood is the main channel through which people convert labor into resources. When that channel breaks — suddenly, structurally, or by force — the safety buffer collapses even if food and shelter aren't yet gone.

needs.title: Health safety net
needs.definition: Recovery infrastructure for injury and illness, and protection from its cost.
needs.description: Threat: illness or injury strikes unpredictably. Without a buffer, recovery costs destroy savings, land, or life itself — turning a biological event into permanent ruin.

needs.title: Disaster / institutional protection
needs.definition: Population-scale shock absorption — the natural event, and the institutional failure to answer it.
needs.description: A buffer against unpredictable future population-scale threats — natural disaster, or institutional failure to respond to one.

needs.title: Information / epistemic security
needs.definition: Access to information true enough to act on, and protection from engineered falsity.
needs.description: The buffer of accurate foresight — knowing what threats are coming in time to act. This is distinct from the threat itself. Attacked by propaganda, censorship, disinformation, and information blackouts, which don't create the famine/plague/war but blind people to it until too late.

needs.title: Mate acquisition / courtship
needs.definition: The ability to find and form a reproductive/intimate partnership at all.
needs.description: Distinct from bond *maintenance*: this is the competing-for phase, where population-level mate-market structure (sex ratios, endogamy rules, price systems) determines whether an individual can find a mate at all. Offspring altriciality forced pair-bonding into the human reproductive strategy; when the market that produces those bonds is distorted, the failure shows up as bachelorhood, coerced marriage, or violence between competitors. This topic is thinner-documented than food or violence — much of the evidence is demographic (sex-ratio data) rather than narrative history, so some entries below lean on statistics more than events.

needs.title: Pair-bonding / marriage
needs.definition: Maintenance of the formed bond, as distinct from forming it.
needs.description: Bonding as a precondition for this species' reproductive/care strategy.

needs.title: Parent-child attachment
needs.definition: Sustained caregiver attachment, which an altricial species depends on to develop at all.
needs.description: Bonding between parent/caregiver and child as a precondition for the species' care strategy — humans are altricial and depend on sustained attachment for survival and development.

needs.title: Kinship / lineage network
needs.definition: Extended-family bonds as the scaled-up form of the parent-child mechanism.
needs.description: Extended-family/lineage bonds as a scaled-up version of the parent-child bonding mechanism.

needs.title: Peer / non-kin community bonds
needs.definition: Durable trust structures beyond blood — village, guild, parish, neighbourhood.
needs.description: Group cohesion as bonding scaled beyond blood ties. Villages, guilds, parishes, and neighborhoods extend trust past kinship into durable peer structures. When those structures are dissolved — by economic transformation, forced movement, war, or withdrawal into private life — people keep kin ties but lose the wider web that made them legible and mutually obligated to non-relatives.

needs.title: Intergenerational transmission
needs.definition: Passing skills, language, practice and obligation from one generation to the next.
needs.description: Continuity of bonding structures across generations: language, craft skill, and social role passed from elder to young. When this chain breaks, a group loses not just information but the medium through which identity and belonging are transmitted.

needs.title: In-group identity / cohesion
needs.definition: The we-feeling that lets strangers act as kin at scale.
needs.description: Group cohesion as a bonding mechanism scaled from blood-kin to symbolic/national in-groups — the "we-feeling" that lets strangers act as kin.

needs.title: Hereditary / caste status
needs.definition: Rank assigned by birth into a hereditary order, gating resource and mating access.
needs.description: Rank gates resource and mating access within a group. When hereditary status closes, esteem stops being convertible into access — provoking either forced leveling or entrenched backlash. History shows four distinct failure modes, not one: sudden legal abolition, slow economic erosion, violent reassertion when loss is threatened, and quiet persistence/adaptation under formal abolition. Colonial administration adds a fifth: outside powers hardening indigenous hierarchies for their own convenience.

needs.title: Ascribed-identity status
needs.definition: Rank assigned at birth by race, sex or origin — no performance can change it.
needs.description: Rank gates resource/mating access within a group. Here rank is assigned at birth — by skin color, sex, or nation of origin — not earned. Ascribed status is the purest form of gatekept esteem: no performance can change it.

needs.title: Economic / class status
needs.definition: Rank held through economic position and its mobility, or absence of it.
needs.description: Rank within a group gates resource and mating access. This file covers how economic/class rank has been suddenly destroyed, inverted, or expropriated — collapsing the status security of whole classes — and what institutions humanity built to dampen that volatility.

needs.title: Occupational / skill status
needs.definition: Rank held through mastery of a craft or profession; its loss reads as identity collapse.
needs.description: Rank gates resource/mating access within a group. Occupational and skill status is a primary rank ladder — mastery of a craft or profession sets a person's place in the group's hierarchy, and loss of that ladder is experienced as identity collapse, not just income loss.

needs.title: Political / power rank
needs.definition: Held position in the lever that decides who eats and who is protected.
needs.description: Rank gates resource and mating access within a group — losing political rank is not symbolic, it is the loss of the lever that controls who eats, who is protected, and who reproduces with advantage.

needs.title: Age / generational rank
needs.definition: Elder-vs-junior privilege, and what happens when the ladder inverts.
needs.description: Rank by age or generation once gated resource and mating access almost everywhere: elders held land, ritual authority, and marriage-approval power over juniors. Industrialization, revolution, colonialism, and demographic aging have each eroded pieces of that gate. This is a thinner record than other esteem-tier threats — the mechanisms below are real but the documentation is sparser and more diffuse than, say, caste or gender rank.

needs.title: In-group vs out-group standing
needs.definition: Rank held collectively — a group's standing against rivals, absorbed by every member.
needs.description: Rank gates resource/mating access. Here rank is held collectively — a nation, empire, or civilization's relative standing against rival groups, not any one individual's. Threats to group standing (defeat, subjugation, humiliation) are absorbed by every member and often outlive the generation that suffered them.

needs.title: Participation / voice
needs.definition: The ability to influence group decisions, which rank neither guarantees nor withholds.
needs.description: Rank gates resource/mating access within a group. Voice is distinct from rank itself — it is the ability to influence group decisions, which can be denied even to people with formal rank (shareholders without board seats) and granted unevenly regardless of rank (a low-status assembly member with one vote still gets a vote). Denial of voice is denial of the ability to shape the rules that determine everyone else's rank.

needs.title: Religious / cosmological meaning
needs.definition: A cosmology that places the self in something that outlasts it.
needs.description: Once survival is secured, the drive to persist/propagate keeps operating but relocates onto symbolic substrates: a cosmology, a god, an afterlife, a chosen people, a sacred order. These decay slower than a body but are still finite — they can be suppressed by states, shattered by conquest, split by schism, undercut by rival science, or simply worn away by secular life. History shows five distinct attack vectors on this substrate: state suppression, forced conversion, internal schism, scientific-cosmological challenge, and gradual secularization.

needs.title: Political / national ideology
needs.definition: Belief systems that supply collective purpose.
needs.description: The drive to persist/propagate points at symbolic constructs — here, political belief systems that give life collective purpose.

needs.title: Occupational / vocational identity
needs.definition: Work as symbolic self-extension — not 'I rank lower' but 'I no longer know what I am'.
needs.description: Work as symbolic self-extension and meaning-source, distinct from Tier 4's status-rank framing of occupation. The threat here is not "I earn less" or "I rank lower" — it is "I no longer know what I am."

needs.title: Ethnic / cultural identity
needs.definition: The symbolic markers — language, script, ritual, place-names — through which a group narrates its continuity.
needs.description: Symbolic self-extension through ethnic/cultural belonging as a meaning-source — distinct from Tier 3's belonging-bond framing, which is about relational attachment, not identity-as-meaning. The threat here is erasure of the symbolic markers (language, script, ritual, dress, place-names, kinship structure) through which a group narrates its own continuity across generations. History shows this threat taking four forms: deliberate state policy aimed at erasure, colonial imposition of foreign categories, forced assimilation short of genocide, and the slower, undirected dilution that diaspora and post-colonial nation-building both produce.

needs.title: Personal legacy / individual purpose
needs.definition: Individual meaning and legacy, distinct from collective ideology or identity.
needs.description: Symbolic self-extension through individual legacy/purpose as a meaning-source, distinct from collective ideology/identity forms.

needs.title: Collective memory / ancestor-continuity
needs.definition: The line back to the dead — record, rite and remembrance.
needs.description: Symbolic self-extension through being remembered and continuing an ancestral chain — distinct from group-membership identity. Threat = severing the chain (destroying records, kin, or the practices that link living to dead and present to future). Response = institutions that fix memory against deliberate erasure.

needs.title: Aesthetic / creative expression
needs.definition: Making, and being able to make, as a meaning-source.
needs.description: Creative and ritual making is symbolic self-extension — a person or people asserting "this form matters" beyond survival need. Because that assertion carries political and cultural weight, it is a recurring target for control: states ban forms that compete with official meaning-making, colonizers suppress rituals that anchor a rival cosmology, industrialization prices out the slow hand-forms that carried aesthetic tradition. Yet the same record shows the drive persisting under extreme deprivation — art made in camps, under bans, in secret — suggesting the need is closer to compulsive than optional.

needs.title: Understanding / comprehension
needs.definition: Curiosity-driven sense-making pursued for its own sake.
needs.description: Symbolic self-extension through curiosity-driven sense-making as a meaning-source — distinct from Tier 2's threat-focused information security, this is comprehension pursued for its own sake.

leaves.title: Ambient asbestos exposure from construction and demolition dust
leaves.one_line: A speculative second exposure route — fibre release from weathering, cutting and demolishing India's in-place asbestos-cement roofing stock as an ambient urban exposure reaching people who never worked with the material. No ambient asbestos-fibre measurement exists for any Indian city, asbestos is not a NAAQS parameter, and that absence is the finding.

leaves.title: Chrysotile asbestos still legally imported and used
leaves.one_line: India banned asbestos mining but left chrysotile import and use fully legal — a third to half a million tonnes a year, mostly roofing sold to poor households. With no disease registry and a 20–40 year latency, India has reported zero mesothelioma deaths to the WHO. The wave arrives in the 2040s.
leaves.gap_note: Representation exists and has existed since 2000 — it has won court rulings and never moved the import trade. The blocker is the asbestos-cement lobby and India's veto at the Rotterdam Convention.

leaves.title: Household air pollution from solid-fuel cooking
leaves.one_line: India put an LPG connection in ~103 million poor kitchens but kept subsidising the connection and not the refill, so roughly a third of households still cook mainly on wood and dung and Ujjwala beneficiaries burn about four cylinders a year against the eight-plus that exclusive clean cooking needs.
leaves.gap_note: the binding constraint is fiscal: clean fuel at this income level cannot be sold without a permanent third-party subsidy for the recurring cost — a programme, not a company — and no institution has committed one at the scale or permanence required. MoPNG holds the lever and operates a placeholder (the 2023 ₹300/cylinder subsidy, set annually, still leaving a meaningful per-cylinder cash cost, refills plateau near 4/year) but treats a deep opex subsidy as an open-ended liability to avoid. Enterprise is not the gap — builders exist for the poor-cashflow delivery instruments (PAYGo LPG metering, 5 kg cylinders, prepaid micro-refills, subsidised induction) but every model collapses without a payer for the recurring cost, so they stay pre-scale or non-Indian. The empty slot is the institutional funder willing to underwrite sustained-use cost, not the delivery instrument. Biogas was run on the same capex-only design for four decades and stalled at ~40% of potential, structurally excluding the landless.

leaves.title: Post-monsoon paddy-straw burning in the north-west
leaves.one_line: Every October–November ~1.7 million paddy farmers in Punjab and Haryana burn ~19 million tonnes of straw in a 10–20-day window because no residue-management option clears at farm-gate prices; the smoke loads the Indo-Gangetic airshed for weeks, downwind of several hundred million people.
leaves.gap_note: coverage on all three legs is present — CAQM is the airshed-scale authority, the biomass co-firing mandate is a working ex-situ offtake lever with straw-to-energy firms behind it (VERBIO, PRESPL, Farm2Energy, A2P, Takachar for biochar), farmer unions organise the source population — but no actor has been catalogued who closes the farm-gate economics of not-burning for a smallholder in a 12-day window; an aggregation-finance / guaranteed-offtake entity that makes in-situ or bale-and-remove cheaper than a match may exist and has not been found. Separately, whole-plant mechanical removal (reaper-binder) has an OEM (Sardar Industries et al.) but no deploying operator, CHC network or subsidy line — a route-level empty slot.

leaves.title: North Indian winter smog
leaves.one_line: The Indo-Gangetic Plain airshed sits year-round far above any health threshold and spikes into multi-week 'severe' PM2.5 episodes every winter, met with an emergency playbook (GRAP, odd-even, school closures) rather than year-round structural source control.
leaves.gap_note: The pollution is airshed-wide: the Indo-Gangetic Plain holds ~40% of India's population, 26–36% of Delhi's winter load blows in from outside the city, and the airshed runs unbroken into three neighbouring countries. It hits outdoor workers and the urban poor hardest — their wages drop when GRAP curbs shut work down. No one represents that unit: CAQM's mandate stops at NCR and its neighbours, with no cross-border power, and the organised activism is Delhi parents acting for their own households. The exposed workforce has no body of its own.

leaves.title: Silica dust exposure and silicosis at national scale
leaves.one_line: An estimated 55 million Indian workers inhale silica dust in quarrying, stone cutting, agate grinding, foundries and construction; states pay compensation once disease is certified but no layer obliges anyone to find the >99% undiagnosed, and the fix needs no ban — only enforcement of controls already on paper.
leaves.gap_note: no one is in the business of finding sick workers before a state medical board certifies them. Quarry workers cannot pay for screening, unorganised employers will not, and no insurer carries the risk. Because money is owed only for certified cases, the bill stays capped at however many are found

leaves.title: Small industrial towns as the worst-air places
leaves.one_line: Loni and Byrnihat — not Delhi — top the world's PM2.5 rankings. Their pollution is made locally, by informal factories and diesel generators too small for the emission rules to reach; at Byrnihat the emitters sit across a state line the local regulator cannot cross.
leaves.gap_note: no affected-led body exists in Loni or Byrnihat (Byrnihat's Feb 2026 factory lock-in shows a latent claimant, no organisation) and the Byrnihat airshed is split across the Assam–Meghalaya line so no single regulator's jurisdiction spans both the emitters and the exposed residents; on the genset sub-source the CPCB IV+/RECD mandate (2023) did manufacture a market (Chakr Innovation, Sudhir Power, EO Energy, Saranya) but keyed to permit-holding facilities, so the informal Loni/Ghaziabad genset base and the town resident are outside it — enterprise is a segment mismatch on gensets and a true absence on informal-cluster combustion

leaves.title: Residual childhood lead exposure (non-petrol sources)
leaves.one_line: The 2000 leaded-petrol phase-out removed the largest source and the effort stopped; ~275 million Indian children — well over half of them — still carry elevated blood lead from adulterated spices, informal battery smelting, paint and cookware, and India runs no blood-lead surveillance to say which children or from what.
leaves.gap_note: no affected-led body exists for lead-poisoned children (the harm is invisible, diffuse, delayed and unattributable by any parent) and no domestic blood-lead-testing market (no payer); institutions hold carrier-fragments (FSSAI the food sample, CPCB the facility) but none has the child as its reporting unit, and the national surveillance programme CSIR/NITI Aayog recommended in 2022 was never built

nodes.title: Construction
nodes.one_line: The construction sector produces shelter while standing as a source of dust, effluent, land conversion, noise and precarious labour, under no single regulator.

nodes.one_line: Generation, grid and fuel supply sit under water pumping, thermoregulation, cooking and food preservation; the mix also sets the ambient combustion load.

mechanisms.title: Aggregation masks failure
mechanisms.one_line: The reporting unit is larger than the harm unit, so the average clears while the affected population does not exist in the data.
mechanisms.description: A statistic is collected at a scale — national, state, city — coarser than the scale at which the harm concentrates, so the mean sits inside the acceptable band while whole sub-populations sit far outside it and never appear as a distinct number. The diagnostic is a compliant headline figure alongside a non-compliant fragment of the same population. The reporting unit needs an owner accountable for the fragment, which makes this an institution problem first — enterprise can move it only where the harmed sub-population can pay to be measured.

mechanisms.title: Spend mismatched to source
mechanisms.one_line: Money is appropriated and executed, but aimed at a contributor other than the load-bearing one.
mechanisms.description: The response is real — funded, staffed, spent on schedule — but attached to a cause that carries a minority of the burden, so effort and outcome decouple. The diagnostic is a well-executed programme whose spending breakdown does not match the causal breakdown of the harm. Fixing it means redirecting the institutional spend to the load-bearing source, or an enterprise serving that source directly; the appropriation already exists, so the barrier is aim, not budget.

mechanisms.title: Instrument keyed to the wrong object
mechanisms.one_line: The remedy attaches to something adjacent to the harm, excluding a class of the harmed by design rather than by failure.
mechanisms.description: A remedy is defined against a proxy for the harm rather than the harm itself, so a class of victims is excluded structurally — the instrument works exactly as written and still misses them. The same shape appears outside the state: in consumer products aimed at the least-affected buyers, and in advocacy built around a claimant group adjacent to the people actually carrying the harm. Because an unserved object concretely exists, enterprise can usually move this one directly.

mechanisms.title: Authority mismatched to harm
mechanisms.one_line: The body with power over the remedy does not contain the source — or is itself the source.
mechanisms.description: The jurisdiction of the body empowered to act does not coincide with the extent of the harm — the harm crosses a boundary the authority does not, or the authority is itself the source — so the entity with power structurally cannot or will not use it. The object needs an owner whose remit matches the harm before either other leg has something to attach to: institution-building first.

mechanisms.title: Primary vs derivative burden
mechanisms.one_line: The visible, contested cause is not the one carrying most of the load.
mechanisms.description: Attention and effort route to the most salient contributor, which is often not the largest, so the majority of the problem is left unaddressed while the minority is fought over. The diagnostic is a heavily contested visible cause that accounts for a small share of the measured load, with a larger, quieter cause beside it. The fix — redirecting to the primary burden — sits with institution or enterprise depending on whether a payer exists.

mechanisms.title: Solution at hand, blocked
mechanisms.one_line: Technically settled and affordable, politically stuck.
mechanisms.description: The technical answer is known, demonstrated and affordable, and the obstacle is entirely political: a concentrated, organised loser against a diffuse, silent beneficiary. This is the one mechanism that meets the frontier criterion by definition — solution at hand, blocker identifiable and movable — and capital cannot shift it; the route is activism into institution.

mechanisms.title: Compensation substitutes for counting
mechanisms.one_line: A payout layer is built without the detection layer beneath it, capping liability by leaving the denominator unknown.
mechanisms.description: The state builds the machinery to pay for a harm without building the machinery to detect it, so the bill is bounded by how few cases are found rather than by how many exist. Paying is politically cheaper than measuring, and the compensation ceiling is also why no detection market forms — a cap is not a demand signal. Enterprise can move it where a buyer for detection exists; otherwise the missing denominator is itself what activism must contest.

mechanisms.title: Within-tier loop
mechanisms.one_line: Secondary. Provision of one need in a tier degrades another in the same tier.
mechanisms.description: Meeting one need with the cheapest available satisfier damages a neighbouring need in the same tier, so the ledger nets out lower than the provision figure suggests. Secondary to the seven, but worth tagging because the second harm is usually uncounted.

mechanisms.title: The second half never built
mechanisms.one_line: Secondary. Collection without treatment, enrolment without teaching, law without the delivery body.
mechanisms.description: The first stage of a two-stage remedy is built and the second is not, so the visible activity — infrastructure laid, people enrolled, a law passed — relocates the problem rather than resolving it. It is the leg-2 → leg-3 handoff failing, and the binding constraint turns out to be executing a won remedy more often than winning it.

mechanisms.title: Visible win strands the residual
mechanisms.one_line: Provisional. A decisive win against the largest, most salient contributor drains the political attention that would have funded action on the diffuse remainder — the residual is left to no one because the headline problem was declared solved. 2 instances so far (residual-childhood-lead, crop-residue-burning).
mechanisms.description: A decisive, well-publicised victory against the largest and most visible contributor removes the political attention that would have funded work on the diffuse remainder, which is then left to no one because the headline problem has been declared solved. It sits below the "3-plus tier-1 files" bar the original seven cleared, so it is carried as provisional pending more instances.

mechanisms.title: Unclassified
mechanisms.one_line: None of the above fits without distortion. A legitimate value, and the leaf owes a §C paragraph saying what the pattern actually is — that paragraph is where the next mechanism comes from.
mechanisms.description: Not a failure of tagging — a required escape value. The seven mechanisms were derived from tier-1 state-instrument failures; tiers 3–5 fail through status hierarchies, kinship arrangements and belief systems, where no instrument is keyed to anything, and forcing that material into the seven produces a confident wrong tag that the cross-leaf view then groups as alike. A leaf tagged unclassified owes a paragraph in its diagnosis section saying what the pattern actually is — that paragraph is where the eighth mechanism will come from.

axes.title: Freedom / autonomy
axes.one_line: Cannot be lost alone — it is the axis every tier is held on, and its failure shows up inside other needs rather than beside them.

axes.title: Leisure / play
axes.one_line: Unclaimed time. Squeezed out of every tier by the provision of the tiers below it.
